headline: New law lets managers of employee stock ownership plans rely on independent appraisals when valuing stock in privately held companies.
what_it_does: This law covers Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs), where workers earn shares of their employer's stock as part of their pay and get the cash value when they leave or retire. When the company's stock is not traded on a public market, the person managing the plan may rely on a value set by an independent appraiser. The appraiser must follow the valuation method laid out in IRS Revenue Ruling 59-60, which lists factors to consider when valuing a privately held business.

who_it_affects.group: ESOP plan fiduciaries (the people who manage these plans)
who_it_affects.how: They may rely on an independent appraiser's valuation when deciding the fair market value of company stock that is not publicly traded.

who_it_affects.group: Workers at privately held companies with ESOPs
who_it_affects.how: The value of the shares in their accounts, and the cash they receive when they leave or retire, will be based on appraisals that must follow set IRS methods.

who_it_affects.group: Independent business appraisers and valuation experts
who_it_affects.how: Their valuations of ESOP stock must follow the methodology in IRS Revenue Ruling 59-60 for plan managers to rely on them.

who_it_affects.group: Privately held companies that offer ESOPs
who_it_affects.how: Their stock will be valued under this standard approach for purposes of their employee ownership plans.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted October 15, 2026; the summary does not state a separate start date.
